#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from PBS

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# PBS resources:
#   -l nodes=1:ppn=12
#   -l vmem=94gb
#   -l walltime=24:00:00
#   -j oe
#   -M briochemc@gmail.com
#   -m abe
#   -e $HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization/cluster_output/run_TimerOutputs_w0.err
#   -o $HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization/cluster_output/run_TimerOutputs_w0.out

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 12
#flux: --time-limit=24h
#flux: --output=$HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization/cluster_output/run_TimerOutputs_w0.out
#flux: --error=$HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization/cluster_output/run_TimerOutputs_w0.err

# Omitted PBS option: -l vmem=94gb
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted PBS option: -j oe (join stdout/stderr)
# Flux commonly manages stdout/stderr separately; a portable join directive is not guaranteed.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but logs may be split.

# Omitted PBS options: -M / -m (email notifications)
# Flux does not provide a universal, built-in email notification directive in batch scripts.
# Performance implication: none on runtime performance, but you will not receive automatic job emails.

module load julia/1.1.0

cd "$HOME/Projects/FastBGCParameterOptimization"

# Set DataDeps environment variable to download without asking
export DATADEPS_ALWAYS_ACCEPT=true

julia src/run_TimerOutputs_w0.jl

reasons: PBS requested 94GB of virtual memory (`-l vmem=94gb`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this can under-provision the job and risk OOM or degraded performance.
